framework.name: NextT-Gym
framework.note: The research gym in gym/ and nextt_gym/ of fork commit c8e3177 (not in upstream main). The agent ran in a container with one CPU and network access and drove the gym only through its MCP tools; the gym trained and calibrated candidates on up to 32 GPUs and returned dev-split values. Besides the repository's method sources, the gym offered the published run records in results/runs/ as history. The candidates' code ran in the gym's training processes without process isolation; the agent received dev-split values only.

researcher.involvementNote: The research session ran without human intervention: the person started it with the gym's task instruction, a budget of 1.96e20 training FLOPs and 32 GPUs, and did not intervene until the agent submitted. The person chose no candidate and gave no directional hint. Afterwards the person asked for this session's submission and those of two other sessions (proposal issues #71 and #72) to be preregistered and trained, and approved the formal launches. Packaging the frozen candidate, calibration, the pre-launch checks, the launches and the audit were operations done by the operator's agent.

research.formalNote: Two launches of the preregistered configuration (fork commit 57b3367, code bundle SHA-256 8289517a…), each on 32 H20 GPUs (4 nodes × 8), 32 ranks, micro-batch 16, no accumulation; neither failed. The first was a planned 44-hour segment: it logged updates up to 43,490 and stopped at its planned timeout; its newest complete checkpoint was 43,000. The second resumed from that checkpoint, re-ran updates 43,001–43,490 (the replayed events are archived and not counted) and finished at 46,875. Preregistration: proposal issue #70, filed on 2026-11-21 at 07:00 UTC, before the first launch at 08:03 UTC.
research.hardware: Up to 32 H20 (4 nodes × 8) for the research; 32 H20 (4 nodes × 8) for the formal run
research.computeNote: Research: 631.97 GPU-hours and 5.58e19 training FLOPs (28.5% of the session budget of 1.96e20), metered by NextT-Gym over 38 jobs (18 calibrations, 4 validations, 15 training jobs of which 2 were cancelled): platform GPU-hours, pod time × GPUs (queueing excluded). Nine distinct designs were trained beyond smoke tests, including the agent's own reproduction of AttnRes-Canon; the submitted candidate is the winning design re-registered with a rewritten hypothesis and trained for 32 updates as a check. Formal: 1,543.45 GPU-hours, pod time × 32 GPUs of the two segments as the cluster recorded it (158,424 s and 15,214 s). Not included: two bounded pre-launch checks on 32 GPUs, a four-node resume check on the dev split (1,160 s) and a two-update smoke run of the CORE evaluation path (295 s), 12.93 GPU-hours together. LLM tokens in the research session: 8.98e7 input (8.34e7 cached) and 3.4e5 output. The agent ran two web searches (the bigram hash embedding of the modded-nanogpt speedrun and nanochat) and read three arXiv papers (2601.07372, 2609.15126, 2610.13630).

closestPrior: Hashed n-gram embeddings (the modded-nanogpt bigram hash embedding; Engram)
novelty.statement: Combines a hashed bigram memory, added to the token embedding, with the AttnRes-Canon trunk, and moves Canon layers onto the depth sources: every block output and the embedding source pass through a causal convolution before any sublayer reads them over depth, and the final depth read has its own. MSAR also applies causal taps to depth sources, but keeps them as separate streams.
